meanings.note: Fixed expression. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to have'.
Très bien = very well, fine. Invariable French adverb meaning 'well'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.
C'est bien. Invariable French adverb meaning 'well'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Très bien. Et vous? Un thé?

meanings.note: determiner: ce soir = tonight, cette semaine = this week
pronoun: c'est = it is; tout ce que = all that

examples.text: Je ne peux pas venir ce soir.
Cette agence ne représente que des stars.
Magali, je dois voir la pièce de Koltès cette semaine.
examples.trans: Magali, I have to see the Koltès play this week.

meanings.note: Une situation complexe. Prefix 'com-' (from Latin 'cum') means 'with, together'.

examples.text: Elle est bien trop complexe pour ça.
examples.trans: She is much too complex for that.

meanings.note: Adjective of capability/quality formed with '-able'/'-ible' (from Latin '-abilis'/'-ibilis').
Adjective of capability/quality formed with '-able'/'-ible' (from Latin '-abilis'/'-ibilis').

examples.text: Je me sens toujours très coupable.
Il n'est pas coupable de cette erreur.
examples.trans: He is not guilty of this mistake.

examples.text: Faire le ménage, c'est un geste coupable.
examples.trans: Cleaning up, it is a guilty move.

meanings.note: Une date de tournage. Feminine noun ('la date', plural 'les dates') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'calendar date'.

examples.text: La prochaine date est le seize juin.
examples.trans: The next date is June sixteenth.

meanings.note: D' before a vowel. Core French preposition meaning 'of', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
le film de Tarantino = Tarantino's film
Also 'some': du sucre. Core French preposition meaning 'of', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
À demain = see you tomorrow. Invariable French adverb meaning 'tomorrow'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Et demain, tu déjeunes avec Audiard.
examples.trans: And tomorrow you're having lunch with Audiard.

meanings.en: to hurry, to rush; se dépêcher = to hurry up
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to hurry'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'dépêché').

examples.text: Il faut se dépêcher, c'est loin.
examples.trans: We must hurry, it is far.
This way, let us hurry up a bit!
Hurry up, the casting is starting now.

meanings.note: for a feminine noun: l'industrie... elle
for a feminine noun: l'industrie... elle

examples.text: Écoute, c'est une industrie, et elle est pleine de requins.
examples.trans: Listen, it's an industry, and it's full of sharks.

meanings.note: en retard = late, en vacances = on holiday

examples.text: Oh non! Je suis en retard.

meanings.note: Essayer de + infinitive. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to try'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'essayé').
Clothes. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to try'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'essayé').

examples.text: J'ai essayé de t'appeler. C'est non-stop au boulot aujourd'hui.
examples.trans: I tried to call you. It's non-stop at work today.

meanings.en: turns a sentence into a yes/no question
meanings.note: est-ce que tu viens? = are you coming?

examples.text: Est-ce que j'ai fait quelque chose de mal?
Est-ce que Rebecca est dans mon agenda?

meanings.note: for (duration): ça fait des mois que j'attends = I've been waiting for months

examples.text: Ça fait une heure que j'attends.
examples.trans: I've been waiting for an hour.

meanings.note: Une fois, deux fois = once, twice. Feminine noun ('la fois', plural 'les fois') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'time'.

examples.trans: I'm going to have lunch twice.

examples.text: L'un à midi, l'autre à quatorze heures. Je vais déjeuner deux fois.
examples.trans: One at noon, the other at two. I'm going to have lunch twice.

meanings.note: Un geste de rébellion. Masculine noun ('le geste', plural 'les gestes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'gesture'.
Un geste de rébellion. Masculine noun ('le geste', plural 'les gestes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'gesture'.

examples.text: Dans le film, c'est un geste de rébellion.
examples.trans: In the film, it's a gesture of rebellion.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le hasard', plural 'les hasards') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'chance'.

examples.text: Nous nous sommes rencontrés dans la rue par hasard.
examples.trans: We met in the street by chance.

examples.text: Dans ce métier, il ne faut rien laisser au hasard.
examples.trans: In this profession, you must leave nothing to chance.

meanings.note: Never changes for plural. Spoken French phrase expression meaning 'there is', common in natural conversation.
il y a trois semaines = three weeks ago

examples.text: Il y a une autre Clémentine?
Non, c'est la place de Samuel. Il est mort il y a six jours.
examples.trans: No, it's Samuel's place. He died six days ago.

meanings.note: J' before a vowel. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'I'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.

examples.text: Gabriel! Je suis à mon cours d'équitation.
examples.trans: Gabriel! I'm at my horse-riding lesson.

meanings.note: definite article; l' before a vowel

examples.text: C'est le prochain film de Tarantino.

meanings.note: Le marché local. Masculine noun ('le marché', plural 'les marchés') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'market'.

examples.trans: I am going to the market.

meanings.note: Laisser un message. Masculine noun formed with the suffix '-age' (from Late Latin '-aticum') denoting an action, state, or collection. Standard masculine noun meaning 'message, text'.

examples.text: Désolé pour tes messages. J'ai été très occupé.
examples.trans: Sorry about your messages. I've been very busy.

meanings.note: faire le ménage = to do the cleaning / housework
Masculine noun formed with the suffix '-age' (from Late Latin '-aticum') denoting an action, state, or collection. Standard masculine noun meaning 'housework, cleaning; household'.

examples.text: Oui, elle fait le ménage pour la duchesse.
examples.trans: Yes, she does the cleaning for the duchess.

examples.text: Je fais le ménage le samedi.
examples.trans: I do the cleaning on Saturdays.

examples.text: Les femmes de ménage et les vacances étaient payées avec l'argent de l'agence.
examples.trans: The cleaners and the vacations were paid for with the agency's money.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la naissance', plural 'les naissances') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'birth'.

examples.text: Nous fêtons la naissance de Flora.
examples.trans: We celebrate the birth of Flora.

examples.text: Il vient pour la déclaration de naissance?
examples.trans: Is he coming for the birth declaration?

meanings.note: everyday speech, with a he/she verb form

meanings.note: before an infinitive: pour faire plaisir
+ infinitive: pour voir. Core French preposition meaning 'for', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

examples.text: Je suis là pour voir Mathias.

meanings.note: starts a question: qu'est-ce que tu fais? = what are you doing?

examples.text: Qu'est-ce que tu fais à Paris?
examples.trans: What are you doing in Paris?

examples.text: Qu'est-ce que tu fais à Paris? Tu es en vacances?
examples.trans: What are you doing in Paris? Are you on holiday?

meanings.note: Spoken French num expression meaning 'four', common in natural conversation.

examples.text: Je peux t'appeler à quatre heures du matin? Tu travailles le dimanche?
examples.trans: Can I call you at four in the morning? Do you work on Sundays?

meanings.note: Joins two parts: dis-lui que. French conjunction meaning 'that', used to link clauses in spoken and written discourse.
Relative: tout ce que. French conjunction meaning 'that', used to link clauses in spoken and written discourse.

Appelle Clémentine. Dis-lui que je ne peux pas venir ce soir.
examples.trans: Call Clémentine. Tell her I can't come tonight.

meanings.note: informal, often at the end: pour faire quoi?, c'est quoi?

examples.text: Quoi, tu n'as pas encore lu le nouveau scénario?
examples.trans: What, you haven't read the new script yet?

examples.text: De quoi est-ce que vous parlez tous les deux?
examples.trans: What are the two of you talking about?

meanings.note: with ne: je ne promets rien; rien n'est signé

examples.text: Rien n'est signé. On attend l'appel.
examples.trans: Nothing is signed. We're waiting for the call.

meanings.note: After the verb. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'alone'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.
Before the noun: le seul agent. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'alone'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Alors je me débrouille seule, comme toujours!
examples.trans: So I'll manage on my own, as always!

meanings.note: agrees with the thing owned, not the owner

examples.text: Oui, trois cent mille. Je parle de ses vingt ans de carrière.
examples.trans: Yes, three hundred thousand. I'm talking about his twenty years of career.

meanings.note: Je vous en supplie = I beg you. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to beg'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'supplié').

examples.text: Donnez-lui une autre chance. Solveig, je vous en supplie.
examples.trans: Give her another chance. Solveig, I beg you.

meanings.note: Sur la table, sur la route. Core French preposition meaning 'on', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
Sur haut-parleur = on speaker. Core French preposition meaning 'on', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

examples.text: Le livre est sur la table.
examples.trans: The book is on the table.

examples.text: Attention, tu arrives sur la route!
examples.trans: Careful, you're heading for the road!

meanings.note: Tout le temps = all the time. Masculine noun ('le temps', plural 'les temps') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'time'.
Quel temps fait-il?. Masculine noun ('le temps', plural 'les temps') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'time'.

examples.text: Mes amies en parlent tout le temps.
examples.trans: My friends talk about it all the time.

meanings.note: takes a singular verb: tout le monde est là

examples.text: On est au Westin. Tout le monde est là.
examples.trans: We're at the Westin. Everyone is here.

meanings.note: Trop vieille = too old. Invariable French adverb meaning 'too'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.
Trop de travail. Invariable French adverb meaning 'too'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Elle est trop vieille pour le rôle.
examples.trans: She's too old for the part.

examples.text: Trop vieille? C'est quoi le rôle, une gamine?
examples.trans: Too old? What's the part, a little girl?

meanings.note: trouver quelqu'un sympa = to find someone nice

meanings.en: trouve quelque chose = think of something
meanings.note: In context. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to find'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'trouvé').

examples.text: Je ne sais pas. Trouve quelque chose.
examples.trans: I don't know. Think of something.

meanings.note: one person you know well: friends, family, close colleagues

examples.text: Deux places pour mardi? Mardi, tu as le film de Kechiche.
examples.trans: Two tickets for Tuesday? On Tuesday you've got the Kechiche film.

meanings.note: Au téléphone = on the phone. Masculine noun ('le téléphone', plural 'les téléphones') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'telephone'.

examples.text: Ah, si! J'ai eu Miranda Jones au téléphone.
examples.trans: Oh, yes! I had Miranda Jones on the phone.

Number; l'un = one of them. Spoken French det expression meaning 'a', common in natural conversation.

examples.text: L'un à midi, l'autre à deux heures.
examples.trans: One at noon, the other at two.

meanings.note: Il y a = there is / there are. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'there'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.
J'y pense = I think about it. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'there'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.

examples.text: S'il vous plaît. Il n'y a rien entre Mathias et moi, d'accord?
examples.trans: Please. There's nothing between Mathias and me, okay?

meanings.note: Place: à Paris, à mon cours. Core French preposition meaning 'at', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
Time: à midi. Core French preposition meaning 'at', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

meanings.en: to annoy, to get on someone's nerves
meanings.note: Ça m'énerve! = that annoys me!. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to annoy'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'énervé').

meanings.en: s'énerver = to get angry, to lose one's temper
meanings.note: ne t'énerve pas = don't get worked up

examples.trans: Julie is getting worked up on the set.

examples.text: Joey, Julie s'énerve. Elle va quitter le plateau!
examples.trans: Joey, Julie is getting angry. She's going to walk off the set!
